newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia seeks multi-stop air rights in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Australia seeks multi-stop air rights in Indonesia.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp signalled on Wednesday that Canberra would seek an agreement with Indonesia to fly passengers to third-country destinations during negotiations for a new air services pact in September.
Sharp said Australia would seek fifth-freedom rights, which allow an airline flying from its home base to a country to pick up passengers before travelling to a third country.
Indonesian and Australian officials are due to meet in September to negotiate a new air services agreement.

"We will do air service agreements on the basis that the airline flies to one destination and can go beyond that to another to really harvest the profitable chances," said Sharp, who is on a two-day visit to Indonesia.
Sharp was due to meet Indonesian Transport Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto and Coordinating Minister for Distribution and Production Hartarto before heading to Japan later on Wednesday.

Passenger traffic between the two countries grew by 15 percent in the past 12 months with an average of 8,100 people travelling between the two countries every week. Last year, the two nations extended air travel capacity by 38 percent for 1997/98.

"For an airline to fly to one destination is not always profitable. It is more profitable if any airline can fly to a destination and go beyond there to another destination," Sharp told members of the Indonesia-Australia Business Council.

"What we need to do with our Indonesian counterparts here is to package up those opportunities so our tourists can get to their destinations at affordable pricing and the airline is given the incentive of finding if there are additional opportunities beyond the initial destination," he said in answer to a question.
